references.text: In [ref:Matt 23:1|Matthew 23:1], Jesus says similar words: "Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples." Matthew's parallel account shows that Jesus addressed both the people and his disciples with his warning against the scribes.
[ref:Mark 12:38|Mark 12:38] is the direct parallel: "In his teaching he said, 'Beware of the scribes…'" Mark describes the same situation where Jesus teaches the crowds and warns against the scribes.

The content of Jesus' speech to the disciples follows in [ref:Luk 20:46-47|Luke 20:46–47], where he warns against the scribes who like to walk around in long robes and wish to be greeted in the marketplaces. Verse 45 introduces this warning.

In [ref:Matt 5:1-2|Matthew 5:1–2], Jesus addresses his disciples specifically while the crowds are present, just as he does here in Luke 20:45—a pattern where Jesus teaches the disciples while the people listen.

In [ref:Luk 12:1|Luke 12:1], Jesus first speaks to his disciples while a large crowd is gathered, warning them against the yeast of the Pharisees (hypocrisy). The same situation as here: Jesus speaks to the disciples in the hearing of the people.
